title: Remission defined: the debt is paid and liability to penalty ceases
source_text: II. Quum debitum illud solvitur, & cessat homo obnoxius esse poenis illis quas justitia divina a peccatoribus exigit, homini peccata remitti dicuntur: retineri vero quamdiu peccator, eorum respectu, manet apud Deum ad poenam obligatus. Adeoque remissio peccatorum in eo consistit, quod qui antea erat a favore Dei exclusus, & poenis quas lex Dei transgressoribus minatur obnoxius, talis esse definit.
pass_a_gloss: When that debt is paid, and the man ceases to be liable to those penalties which divine justice exacts from sinners, sins are said to be remitted to the man: but they are said to be retained as long as the sinner, with respect to them, remains bound before God to punishment. And so the remission of sins consists in this, that he who before was shut out from God’s favor, and liable to the penalties with which God’s law threatens transgressors, ceases to be such.
pass_b_english: Remission = the debt paid and penalty-liability ended; retention = still bound to punishment.
So pardon is the end of exclusion-from-favor and of law-threatened obnoxiousness.

choices.why: Defined as cessation of penalty-liability, not a bare decree-word.
